title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: misdeclaration findings, penalty and inspection cost recovery
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product, when the line's inspection finds that the goods in a container differ from the signed declaration in UN number, class or packing group, the shipper is charged the category's misdeclaration penalty for each affected container, capped at the category's penalty cap per acceptance, plus the category's inspection cost recovery once. The finding is a system record of the inspection department; a customer's statement that the declaration was correct never removes it. A misdeclaration penalty may be booked only on an acceptance that is approved, loaded, discharged or closed. Each charge code is charged at most once per acceptance. Misdeclaration penalties and inspection costs are never waived by the desk, and an appeal against the finding is decided by the dangerous-goods department, not the desk. A penalty blocks the customer's new applications under the admission rules.

## Calculation in words
- **Penalty**: the lower of the per-container penalty multiplied by the number of affected containers, and the cap per acceptance.
- **Inspection cost recovery**: the category's figure, charged once per acceptance.
The two are separate charges on the acceptance.

## Worked cases (hypothetical rates: 20000.00 per container, cap 90000.00, inspection 400.00)
| Affected containers | Per-container penalty multiplied by containers | Penalty charged | Inspection cost recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 60000.00 | 60000.00 (below the cap) | 400.00 |
| 6 | 120000.00 | 90000.00 (capped) | 400.00 |

## When the penalty may be booked
| Acceptance status | Penalty may be booked |
|---|---|
| approved, loaded, discharged or closed | yes |
| any other status | no |

## Points of judgement
- *The customer insists the goods were declared correctly — does that cancel the finding?* No; the finding is the inspection department's system record.
- *May the desk waive the penalty or the inspection cost?* No; they are never waived by the desk.
- *Who decides an appeal against the finding?* The dangerous-goods department, not the desk.
